The Secretariat of the Convention on the Conservation of Migratory Species of Wild Animals would like to highlight an important opportunity for strengthening synergies between the UNCCD and CMS on sustainable pastoralism. Migratory species depend On connected functional ecosystems, pasture lands and migratory species habitats often overlap, but the relationship between pastoralists and wildlife is complex. Many migratory birds and mammals benefit from sustainably used rangelands, which can maintain diverse ecosystems, prevent their conversion to other forms of land use, which can be unsuitable for wildlife. However, overgrazing by livestock and human wildlife conflict greatly contribute to land degradation as well as to the loss of biodiversity, including migratory species. At its 15th meeting held in Campo Grande, Brazil earlier this year, the CMS Conference of the Parties adopted a set of decisions on pastoralism and migratory species, notably CMS COP 15 Decision 15. 205 gives the CMS Scientific Council's Working Group on Pastoralism an explicit mandate to cooperate with the UNCCD Secretariat. It is tasked with preparing recommendations on sustainable pastoralism in migratory species habitat and advising how these recommendations can be mainstreamed into land use and conservation policies at national and international levels. with the objective of achieving benefits both for the conservation of migratory species and for pastoralist communities. As many of the delegates attending COP17 are working both on sustainable land use management and on the conservation of migratory species and landscapes, I would like to bring this mandate to the attention of the meeting. We hope that addressing these issues in a synergistic way will help to advance the protection of migratory species of wildlife, pastoral livelihoods and prevent land degradation in the coming years into Alia through implementation of the CMS COP 15 decisions on pastoralism and UNCCD COP 17 decisions on rangelands and pastoralists. Distinguished delegates, at the meeting of the Bureau of the Conference of the Parties on the 24th of February 2026, Germany, on behalf of the European Union and its member states, requested the inclusion of the review of the progress in the implementation of the UNCCD communication plan as an item on the agenda of the COP at its 17th session. To facilitate the deliberations on this agenda item, the Secretariat has prepared document ICCD/COP17/CRP.1 as a conference room paper. In this context, I'm very pleased to introduce this document, which reports on the progress made to date in the implementation of the Communication Plan, the successes and the challenges of the biennium. This conference room paper provides an overview of the activities undertaken by the Secretariat and presents a forecast of the intended focus of communications activities for 2027-2028. In addition to the information contained in document ICCD/COP17/INF/4, titled Report on the Performance of Convention Institutions and Subsidiary Bodies 2025-2026. The present document, CRP1, presents progress in the implementation of the decision 4/COP15, which outlines the work carried out in the implementation of the communication plan, highlighting various campaigns and outreach activities, including yearly desertification and drought day observances. It further provides background information on ongoing media outreach and digital engagement, as well as efforts to mobilize new and influential voices in support of the Convention. This document contains additional information on the planned focus of communications activities in the next biennium. It should be further underscored that the vast majority of the communications activities carried out by the Secretariat are funded through voluntary contributions and I would like to take this opportunity to acknowledge the generous support from Parties and other partners in this area. Finally, it should be noted that in the absence of a specific mandate from COP16, the Secretariat has not prepared any elements of a draft decision for the Parties' consideration on this agenda item. The COP is therefore invited to consider the information on the status of implementation of UNCCD Communication Plan as contained in document ICCD/COP17/CRP.1 and take further actions as appropriate. Thank you, Mr. Chair.

COP17 President, Excellencies, distinguished delegates and representatives. The European Union and its member states recognize the essential role of the UNCCD communication activities in effectively reaching a broader audience, promoting awareness and understanding on desertification, land degradation and drought, as well as the scientific knowledge built by works of the UNCCD. The European Union and its 27 member states thank the Secretariat for providing information on the review of progress in the implementation of the UN CCD communication plan. We also thank the Secretariat for specifically referencing linkages to communication activities set out in other background documents related to the broader COP17 agenda. This highlights the importance of the communications plan in supporting the mandate of the UNCCD by raising the visibility of land issues on political and public agendas. We welcome the continued increase in media and social media reach, the significant increase in website visits, as well as the further expansion of UNCCD communication and outreach activities to a broader non-English speaking audience, We acknowledge the role of the UNCCD land and goodwill ambassadors in providing their support and advocacy behind key UNCCD events and outreach activities, including the Her Land campaign on women's land rights. We also welcome the specific efforts in engaging with women and youth and promoting success stories, as well as the efforts to engage more broadly with pastoralists in the year of rangelands and pastoralists, including via the Silk Road Caravan Campaign. We further encourage the Secretariat to build upon this focus to other priority audiences, including policy makers, line ministries in charge of land-based sectors, the civil society organizations and the private sector, including landowners, land managers and smallholder farmers. We welcome the innovative efforts to reach broader audiences, including by linking communications to major international sporting events, including the African Cup of Nations and World Cup. In the European Union and its member states view, it is essential to systematically incorporate gender awareness raising into the trainings and capacity building activities. As regards the direction of communication activities for the next biennium, the EU and its member states would like to stress the following priorities. It is crucial that the core of the UNCCD activities, including its communication, remain on implementing the UNCCD 2018-2030 strategic framework in its entirety and fulfilling ambitions for the achievement of LDN and drought resilience, focusing on promoting existing science-based work initiatives and action on the ground. We further support the mobilization of scientific and technical data, including information and policy recommendations from the science policy interface, the Global Land Outlook, the Economics of Land Degradation Initiative, the World Overview of Conservation Approaches and Technologies, and other major scientific assessments. In light of this year's triple COPs, the European Union and its member states strongly advocate for communication activities in coordination with climate change and biodiversity communities and providing a consistent message with the other Rio conventions with a view to ensuring synergies and maximum benefit in achieving shared objectives. We welcome reference to these synergies in the note published by the Secretariat. In light of the challenging budgetary situation, in our view, it is essential that the budget dedicated to communication activities and outreach does not negatively impact the available budget for the core activity of the convention. We hence believe available resources in the secretariat should be focused on the most effective communication tools in terms of audience reached relative to the costs incurred, should capitalize on the initiatives and resources already developed, and remain closely linked to the overall narrative on LDN. to safeguard consistent, clear and coherent messaging about the convention. We recall that outcome eight on the UNCCD results framework as contained in the annex to COP16 decision one relates to a bigger profile for the UNCCD on the global agenda through strategic communications and note the proposed increase in allocation to the program of communications, external relations and partnerships compared to the approved budget for this program in 2025 to 2026. We would like to stress the importance of transparency in relation to ongoing implementation of the communications plan and associated expenditure, both in relation to associated human resources and overall program spend. We therefore would welcome the opportunity for further updates on the implementation of the communications plan at future sessions of the COP in relation to the integrated budget under the agenda item on the work program and budget for the biennium. Thank you very much.
